title: Bourbon Vanilla Tallow Balm: What Actually Happened to My Skin
body:
Look, my skin was just being a jerk. This was maybe April? The weather was doing that thing where it’s sunny but the air is still kind of dry and cold, and my face decided to freak out. It wasn’t like, medical-level bad. Just tight. And flaky around my nose. And my hands, god, my hands looked like a lizard’s. I was using that CeraVe cream from the tub, the one everyone says is amazing. It was fine. It was just sitting there. Doing nothing. My skin drank it up and was still thirsty five minutes later. I tried that La Roche-Posay Lipikar stuff too, the big bottle. Felt like I was smearing on a nice, expensive layer of nothing. I was annoyed. And I was scrolling on my phone one night, probably procrastinating on laundry, and I saw someone talking about tallow balm. Beef fat. For your face. I remember thinking, “Okay, that’s a step too far even for me.” But my skin was so… beige. In a bad way. Dull. Unhappy. So I got curious. I found this little Etsy shop that made a whipped tallow balm, and they had a bourbon vanilla scent. Sounded less intimidating. I figured if I was gonna smear cow fat on myself, it should at least smell good. I ordered it. I was fully prepared for it to be a weird, greasy mess.

## How I Even Got to Putting Beef Tallow on My Face

So the jar showed up. It’s small. Cute, actually. Made in France, it said on the label. I opened it. Texture was weird. Not bad weird. It’s whipped, so it’s like this super dense, kind of creamy paste? It’s solid but if you put your finger in, it gives way. It’s not hard. It’s not soft. It’s its own thing. Smelled like vanilla maybe? Or not. Something. It’s a warm smell. Not like cake vanilla, more like… the vanilla bean you’d smell in a fancy store. With something else underneath. Cozy. That’s the word. It just smelled cozy. I was sitting at my kitchen table, it was like 8 PM, and I just went for it. Dabbed a little on my cheek. Rubbed it in. Here’s the thing I wasn’t ready for: it disappeared. Like, it melted. My skin just ate it. No greasy film. No shiny residue. My face just felt… calm. Not “moisturized” in that heavy, product-y way. It just felt like my skin, but not thirsty anymore. I was confused. In a good way.

This is a tangent but the whole “grass-fed beef suet” thing made me think of my grandpa. He had this old tin of something he’d use on his leather work gloves. Probably was just lard. He swore by it. Maybe he was onto something with the whole animal fat thing. Anyway.

## Why This Tallow Stuff Actually Makes Sense for Dry Skin

I looked it up after, because I was so surprised it worked. The science, or whatever, is that beef tallow is kinda close to the oils our own skin makes. Sebum. So it gets it. It doesn’t just sit on top like a silicone blanket pretending to help. It goes in. It tells your skin it can chill out. For someone with skin that’s just dry and sensitive and kind of pissed off at modern life, that’s a big deal. It’s not a 12-step routine. It’s one thing. I started using it at night. After I wash my face, I just take a tiny scoop, warm it between my fingers, and press it into my skin. Around my eyes, my forehead, everywhere. My fine lines around my eyes? I don’t wanna say they’re gone, that’s crazy. But they look… less angry. Hydrated. The skin there doesn’t feel like paper anymore.

And my hands. Oh man. I keep a little sample pot by the sink. After I do dishes, I slather it on. The cracks I used to get on my knuckles in spring? Gone. They just stopped. It heals the dry patches overnight. I used it on my lips once when my usual Burt’s Bees was MIA. Worked better. It’s this weird, all-purpose skin fixer. I got one for my mom because her skin gets so dry in the spring wind, and she texted me last week like “what is this magic?” I didn’t have an answer. It’s just whipped cow fat and vanilla. From France.

## My Skin After a Few Weeks of This Stuff

So it’s been a month maybe. I’m almost out of the jar, which is annoying because I don’t wanna run out. The results aren’t dramatic in a “whoa you look 20 again” way. It’s subtler. My skin just behaves now. It doesn’t get that tight feeling at 3 PM. The flakiness is history. It has this… health? It looks even. Rested. I don’t wake up with dry patches. I used to put on foundation and it would cling to every dry spot. Now it just goes on. Smooth. I sound like an ad but I’m not, I swear, I’m just someone who tried a weird thing and it worked.

I keep forgetting to mention the scent. The bourbon vanilla. It’s not strong. It’s there when you open the jar, and for a minute after you put it on, and then it fades. It’s not perfume-y. It’s just a nice, warm, comforting smell that makes the whole process feel a little more luxurious than “rubbing animal fat on your face.” Which, let’s be honest, is what you’re doing. But it feels good. It feels simple.

## Would I Buy This Tallow Balm Again?

Yeah. I already did. I ordered a second jar last week. And a bigger one for my hands. For natural skincare, it’s the only thing that’s ever made a visible, tangible difference for my dry skin that didn’t cost a fortune or come in fancy packaging. It’s just a little glass jar. I got mine from this Etsy shop, “PureTallowCreations” or something like that. They just make the stuff. No big brand, no influencers. It’s just… good.

It’s not for everyone. If the idea of tallow freaks you out, you won’t get past it. But if your skin is being difficult, and the usual drugstore stuff isn’t cutting it, it might be worth a shot. A weird, beefy, vanilla-scented shot. My elbows haven’t been this smooth since I was a kid. I don’t know what else to say.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Weirdly, yes. Because it’s so similar to the oils our skin already makes, it absorbs really well instead of just clogging the surface. It’s like giving your skin something it actually recognizes and knows how to use.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Not in my experience. And I’m prone to getting clogged pores. It melts right in. It’s not like putting Vaseline on your face. It’s more like a super nutrient-dense oil that your skin drinks up.

**What does the bourbon vanilla tallow balm smell like?**
It’s warm. Like a vanilla bean, not vanilla extract. There’s a depth to it. It’s not sweet. It’s cozy and kind of comforting. The smell doesn’t stick around all day, which I like.

Anyway. If your skin’s being a pain, might be worth a look. It just works.
